summary: Bradford's posts consistently frame small businesses and main streets as central to Toronto's economy and recovery, calling for tax relief, reduced red tape, faster permitting, and pro-growth policy. Bradford repeatedly proposed a 25% small business property tax reduction (DUIl3M_Dx5X, DHW7KI5yH9x, DF5xWk4SBYU, C3GD7yhgljQ), advanced patio and CaféTO reforms (DMgZzjFSD9Y, DMPy-G5Aj9a, CWHEJK1LojO), and championed the Live Music on Patios pilot, Music Strategy, and a small business tax subclass (CWGjlUrAK0K, Ca7-yGhOnRJ). During COVID, Bradford pushed commercial eviction moratoria, rent relief, and Digital Main Street (B_pzUK_lvzP, CBLtqufh7QQ, CEFNZ5ihH2t). On tariffs, Bradford urged using reserves and tax cuts to protect 127,000 manufacturing jobs (DF7o2skxQ5R, DGyGAp0yfRv). Bradford opposed rideshare caps (C3p_JTpA7p_) and supported neighbourhood retail and tech/innovation investment (CgQMAZBLTvL, DP2KMVrDXwv).

key_positions.stance: Supports a 25% property tax reduction for small businesses (and manufacturers), funded without raising homeowner costs.
Supports cutting red tape and getting City Hall to 'yes faster' on permits for small businesses and entrepreneurs.
Supports reforming the patio/CaféTO permit system, including a 25% objection threshold rather than a flat two objections.
Supports making CaféTO permanent and waiving permit fees, and continuing patio/main-street public space programs.
Supports tariff response measures including using reserves, cutting industrial property taxes, and protecting 127,000 manufacturing jobs.
Supports Toronto becoming the most attractive city for business, capital, and innovation, including tech and startups.
Supported COVID-era commercial eviction moratoria and rent relief for small businesses.
Supports a small business property tax subclass distinct from large commercial properties.
Supports allowing small-scale neighbourhood retail (15-minute neighbourhood) and live music venues/programs.
Opposes Mayor Chow's rideshare cap and characterizes it as harmful to drivers earning extra income.
